basis: Muscle-origin mesenchymal neoplasm; cardiac and other site-specific involvement is not shared across the umbrella.
Odontogenic epithelial tumor; about 90% arise within jaw bone, directly occupying and destroying it. The skin-neoplasm parent does not match the definition.
Seizures and hemiparesis establish neurologic disease; the sparse description gives insufficient detail on hemiatrophy or skeletal damage to assign another axis.
Viral hemorrhagic disease; hepatitis and GI hemorrhage from intestinal injury are each frequent (30-79%). Rash and conjunctival signs do not establish lasting injury.
Adenocarcinoma originating in the cecal glandular epithelium.
Peritoneal fibrocollagenous encasement directly impairs the small intestine and causes recurrent obstruction.
Irritant-associated intrinsic asthma affects the airways; the supplied definition does not establish an allergic or other specifically immune-mediated mechanism.
Degeneration of thoracic intervertebral disks; neurologic compression is not intrinsic to every case.
Developmental delay and brain anomalies define disease; exotropia and ptosis each occur in 1/3. Microtia and flat feet lack documented functional injury.
The Westphal variant of Huntington disease is a predominantly rigid-akinetic neurodegenerative disorder.
Combined immunodeficiency with dysfunctional immunity despite the presence of T and B cells; no common additional organ injury is established.
CD8 lymphocytic infiltration characteristically damages salivary glands; pulmonary lymphocytic infiltration occurs in roughly 30%. Renal and nerve injury are less common.
Congenital abnormal pulmonary venous drainage is a cardiovascular malformation; pulmonary parenchymal disease is not shared across the group.
Inherited apolipoprotein deficiency alters triglyceride and cholesterol metabolism; no direct additional organ damage is established.
Disease of the tongue, which belongs to the mouth and gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance, with associated cardiac structural and conduction abnormalities.
Glycosylation disorder; regression, seizures, brain atrophy and limb joint contractures occur in 1/1 reported patient. The frequency estimate rests on a single case.
Mature B-cell lymphoma; extranodal sites vary across subtypes, with insufficient evidence that one additional organ meets the threshold across the umbrella.
MFRP-related microphthalmia with retinal degeneration, foveoschisis and reduced visual acuity; manifestations are ocular.
Presynaptic neuromuscular-junction disease; arthrogryposis and fixed limb contractures occur in 1/1. Bulbar and respiratory weakness do not establish gut or lung injury.
The definition explicitly includes irreversible exocrine and endocrine pancreatic damage. Overt diabetes is occasional (5-29%); thrombosis and pleural complications do not qualify.
Familial focal epilepsy arising from mesial temporal networks; a normal MRI does not negate neurologic dysfunction.
Nonsyndromic dentin defect damages teeth. Frequent joint hypermobility alone does not establish joint damage; hearing impairment is very rare (1-4%).
Enterococcal bacterial infection; the concept specifies no anatomical site, and sites vary across cases.
Trichilemmal cyst arises from the outer hair-root sheath, usually in scalp skin.
